To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the firing rate regulation in dopamin­ergic cells is affected in Parkinson's disease.
the regulation of firing rate of nigrostriata dopamine cells is mainly of a renewal nature, and that the no‐renewall regulation is mainly found in dopamine cells and only in a minority of GABA cells.

(1) two different mechanisms regulate the firing rate of dopaminergic neurons; (2) the partial degeneration in the nigrostriata system affects the regulation of the firing rate; and (3) this disturbance could be one of several factors involved in the motor fluctuations of advanced Parkinson's disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the regulation of firing in DA cells and the mechanisms involved in this regulation, which are important for understanding the firing pattern of DA cells and the motor fluctuations observed in Parkinson's disease.
the mechanisms of firing rate regulation in nigral dopaminergic cells and their possible alterations in Parkinson's disease.
the study of the regulation of firing rate in dopaminergic and non‐dopaminergic nigral cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
renewal regulation is a common property of DA cells, while no‐renewation is a property of a subpopulation of these cells.

the renewal mechanism for firing rate regulation is a common characteristic of the dopaminergic system, and the no‐renewality mechanism is more specific to the DA system, since it is found in a large number of DA cells but not in GABA cells.
DA neurons are not only able to fire in a regular fashion but are also capable of compensating for fluctuations in their firing rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the firing regulation mechanisms in DA cells are very robust, but the no‐renewality mechanism is the most sensitive to the partial degeneration in the nigrostriatum, which is the most affected in advanced Parkinson's.
renewal regulation is a mechanism that prevents the occurrence of short or long ISIs, whereas no‐renewality compensates for the long and short ISIs.
the renewal regulation of DA cells is a mechanism that prevents short and long ISIs and that the no‐renewation mechanism compensates the long ISIs with the short ISIs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the renewal mechanism of regulation is a fundamental feature of the DA system, and that its disturbance could play a significant role in the development of motor fluctuations in advanced Parkinson's.
the regulation of the firing rate of DA cells is a complex process involving two mechanisms, one of a renewal and the other of no‐renewation nature.
firing rate regulation in DA cells is not only a mechanism for the control of firing rate but also a mechanism for the regulation of dopamine concentration.
